A very good alternative to Diablo IV and PoE. It's a happy middle-ground between both games!
Tons of variety, and just plain fun to play. It's still in Beta, so do expect a few bugs, but so far it's been a very smooth and enjoyable experience.

+ Unique, fun classes
+ Legendary items FEEL legendary
+ Entertaining moment-to-moment gameplay

- No character customisation (Could be a deal breaker for some)
- A few minor bugs
- Inventory management can be annoying (But there's a plethora of loot filter options to use!)

NOTE IF YOU EXPERIENCE CRASHES:

I'm not sure if this is useful to anyone here, but I solved my game crashing on login by putting the graphical preset to Very Low and just changing all the other individual settings to the highest (also if you're on a laptop, the game defaults to the integrated GPU). I'm putting it here in case it helps anyone.

This is my first arpg and I'm having a really good time. There are a lot of mechanics I'm not used to in games and Last Epoch has done a really good job explaining everything. If you are new to the genre it is a good game to dive in with, but it seems like it would be good for veterans too.

My only complaint is the lack of achievements. I wish they were there.

Last Epoch is a game of potential.

I think comparing it to Path of Exile, or Diablo, or Grim Dawn, or whatever game you have your heart with is a bit disingenuous. Sure it has elements and similarities, but honestly this game has it's own identity. It isn't simple, but it is accessible.

The classes have a lot of potential and a distinct identity, and they all have a variety of ways to play them. The world is massive with a pretty good roster of monsters and bosses and mechanics. The items and crafting is interesting and has enough depth to keep you engaged without getting too frustrated trying to get a character to a specific strength. It isn't the fastest paced arpg, but it isn't slow. The time travel mechanic is fun and refreshing as a way to break up the world and different challenges it poses.

I think the biggest factor to this game's success is going to be two things: How multiplayer is implemented and supported, and sticking to it's own identity. As long as this game focuses on it's vision without worrying about what people think it should be, then I think it could be a truly great game to play.

Ultimately I enjoy it a lot, and if you are a long-time fan of arpg's you should try it out for yourself. Just don't try to use it as a replacement for what you wish you had, enjoy it as the game that it is.
Excelent game, gameplay, build options, skill tree and loot filter is just amazing and with a lot of replayability! Can´t wait for next month play the new 2 masteries...

I think the game looks beautiful. It runs smoothly.
Combat needs something, its not satisfying yet. It doesn't feel like I'm hitting hard or that some spells have any punch. the map levels are small between jumps/loading screens. seems kind of feels lacking in exploration within a zone. minimap works well, over map is great looking but sometimes i want an expanded mini map to look at.
items comparisons are great! the menus look amazing and clean. the send materials to forge button is very nice. wish other games had this mechanic. not loving the shift click to sell items, nor the lack of value items hold. Equiping seems slow as well.
I find myself skipping dialogue and just clicking the quest line. so i can move forward.
so far its looking good but need those finishing touches.

Game runs great, but initial load takes a long while. If you like PoE you will really enjoy Last Epoch. Its pretty much PoE, but instead of skill gems and finding slotted gear....you have a skill tree connected to each of your skills, and you level your skills up. Solid ARPG, lacking endgame options but still see myself going from 38 to 100+ hours easily. Worth the EA pricetag.

Awesome ARPG, industry leading in terms of quality of life features. Been blasting this season and running alts, something I've never done in a seasonal ARPG before as I'll pick one character and min max it to i get bored usually. Endgame has been expanded vastly this update which was one of the weakest parts previously with the whole weaver faction/woven echo system adding far more variety to the endgame monolith system, and crafting has somehow been made even better, allowing you to really chase that best in slot gear piece you after with a great risk/reward system to it that keeps crafting engaging but also not to easy or to hard to get gear with desired affixes on it for your build.

This game probably falls somewhere between Diablo 4 and POE 2 in terms of difficulty and complexity of game systems, but is easily the most fun and rewarding based on time invested. The corruption system in Monoliths allows you to make the endgame as hard or easy as you want, with the higher you push resulting in far greater item rarity.

Game is a genuine joy to play. Solid 9/10 and looking forward to continuing to blast, and future updates to come.

Do you find that Path of Exile's talent tree confuses the hell out of you?
Want to play a game that has a bit more speed to it then that of Grim Dawn?
Feel that Diablo 1-3 are a bit on the dated side now?

Well, look no further because Last Epoch is giving that rather sweet middle ground on all games and brings a great deal of fun with it! The talent trees are easy to understand, the skill based system allows for a vast amount of customisation and... there is more to come!

Absolutely fantastic ARPG with more depth than Diablo, but not so much that you need a spreadsheet or external app just to plan your character growth out like in Path of Exile. As someone who has spent enough time playing the Diablo franchise to earn a freakin' degree, I can safely say that Last Epoch is one of the best alternatives in existence.

Great arpg, endgame is also pretty well done and easy to grind. Crafting and highest end gear can be confusing to be acquired. It does not matter much if you are a casual player and just want to play the campaign and then have fun in some higher tiers for a while.

Youtube is out there to help you if you are interested in getting truly OP. The community is also quite nice.
Combat feels great, it's well optimized and runs fluent. A few bugs here and there but nothing game breaking and they are working on it. Multiplayer works fine.

A hidden gem with incredible design choices for itemization, crafting and late game progressions that both diablo4 and poe2 have decided to steal ideas from it.

Only downside of it is that due to being a new game in the genre, it is lacking end game content and having trouble with player retention.

Definitely check it out and keep an eye on it for more updates and play it once in a while to show support to developers.

As a very much a casual in ARPG games, I can say I definitely enjoyed and had a lot of fun playing this game!

I played a Marksman in 0.8 and a Druid in 1.0.
As a person that likes to figure out builds themselves, I found that the skill trees and the passive system are not too complicated and it's pretty intuitive to figure out what would combo well for a specific build.

Passive respeccing is pretty much free, it costs just a bit of gold to return a point so you can experiment freely. Skill tree wise it's slightly more involved as you can lose a few skill points you need to regrind if you want to try something else in the tree or select another skill to use its tree but don't let that stop you trying out what you'd think would be cool!

The combat itself is pretty satisfying and chonky.

While I haven't really reached the end game as at this point I'm quite satisfied with how my character turned out (it's pretty much just hunting for better gear now), my builds managed to reach the half way point of normal monoliths and could probably go further.

So yeah, definitely had fun with it so far, I would definitely try out a new class in the future :D

PS: the servers have been behaving well for the last few days at least

Last epoch has a lot of potential to be a game I can come back to every time there's a new cycle and a game in which I can pour hundreds of hours into, but it's in current state that's not the case. Last epoch has a lot of mechanics that artificially impede your progress to make the game a slog to get through in the end game. To get BIS items or even decent endgame ones requires a player to get lucky outcomes on several mechanics 2-3 times in a row. A 10-15 hr grind for a single item can end up with a bricked unusable item. The mechanics for progressing monoliths (the end game mechanic) are also made in a way where you have to go through the most mind numbing grind to get wanted corruption, drops, blessings, etc. The game is extremely rough around the edges with it's mechanics and not to mention bugs (especially when playing in party). If these edges are smoothed out I can see myself putting thousands of hours into this game over the next couple years.
There is some room for improvement, but so far the game is very fun, I really cant wait for the cosmetic options however, curious to see what kinda of mogs they introduce.

You will also hit a wall if you keep playing and only consider damage stats on items, as you will start being stunned to death, one shot or likewise. Once you get further in the game, and get the hang of the itemization, it really starts to pick up. The end-game modes easily gets repetitive, so I would mostly recommend it to players who like gear-chasing & build crafting.

Last Epoch showed great promise from the moment it came out in Early Access and now it has finally hit its stride with the Season 2 "Tombs of the Erased" patch. Today it is an amazing game, easy to get into, with endless content to explore and so many side activities crammed into each and every map you visit that it stays and feels fresh for a long, long time. I highly recommend it, and I cannot wait to see the extra content that future seasons and patches will add to it.

If you've played Path of Exile this game will feel very similar to you. The gameplay is fun, but the lack of build diversity is the major reason I can't recommend the game. The whole reason to play these type of games is to try and see how much synergy you can get with your build in order to climb in-game leaderboards (which are already implemented.) You can choose between 5 classes and 3 'mastery' subclasses for each class. But you CANT change the mastery sub-class once selected around 5 hours into the game.

Because the choice is permanent, new players are stuck making a decision with implications they don't understand. And forced to re-level the same character to try out a different type of mastery. Long term players are expected to understand the different masteries and as the meta shifts they will have to create whole new characters just to experience the same dull story to get to unlock the same thing with slightly different abilities.

It's a glaring issue that in no way benefits the people investing their time into playing this game. If that kind of experience is what this studio is pushing for as the player experience, stay well away. Nothing good will follow suit.

The graphics and sound quality is top notch with easy to learn game play mechanics that will make anyone feel at ease. You can easily respec into your class special classes and refund points as much as you want which makes leveling a breeze. This is a must for die hard fans and new comers alike.
10/10

This game has a very nice story; one of the most unique plot (and partially gameplay) mechanics I've seen in the form of traveling between different eras; revisiting the same locations in different states; some of the quest even requiring you to go to the same places in a different time to unlock access to them, yadda yadda.

I have 400+ hours in this game, but that's not because the story takes 400 hours to finish. No, if you know what you're doing and you don't stall, even without skipping any story, text, or lore, I don't think the entire storyline would take any more than several hours to finish.
However, because of this game's passive trees and skill trees, which are both remarkable, the replayability is ACTUALLY endless. There are only 5 playable characters at the moment, and yet I think this game has more content than the likes of Grim Dawn, Torchlight, POE and especially Diablo 2-3. (Can't say anything in comparison to 4, haven't played it.)

If like me, the part that hooks you most in ARPGs is making builds, experimenting with different skills and characters and trying to make something absolutely broken, gimmicky, or just hilarious to play—this is the game for you.

P.S. don't play acolyte and take mastery into Lich and build everything around poison and DOT or you WILL one shot the entire game including yourself in the process. (Don't do this in hardcore I beg)

Played it for quite some time, made it to endgame on void knight, waiting for warlock now. It is nice alternative to PoE, it is much less complex game and easier to jump to. I have not really experienced any game breaking bugs, just a few crashes in the 100 hours I played.

Currently they released MTXs with oof awkward high pricing for what they look like and also higher packs don't include previous packs, eh??? But since you literally don't need to have MTX to play the game w/e

Wish I could give a "so-so" rating.

It feels like it has some really good foundations to build on, especially compared to Diablo, without getting as absurd and complex as Path of Exile. I genuinely think it is a "good" game.

But it has a few flaws, namely in gearing, leveling alts and class imbalancing. I think after another season or two of effort we could have something very special. I'd give it a look then rather than now.

Last Epoch has a lot of promise and feels like it could be a worthy successor to the Diablo franchise. The variety of skill and talent paths look like they'll provide a lot of replayability.

At the moment, though, the game crashes for me every 20 minutes or so. There's no "save" button, so after a crash you start back to the last place where you exited the game. Every few crashes, it loses all my characters.

I recommend keeping an eye on the game, but holding on to your $35 until they make it playable.

Update after the May 8th patch: got a bit farther before crashing, but still lost my character. The first few levels are fun but it'd be nice to see what comes after.

Slightly generic loot based rpg, class skills feel satisfying but could user further specialization options. Once you get past choosing ur speciality your playstyle is definitely railroaded into a set number of possible skill combinations and passive abilities. Loot is definitely unsatisfying, with high amounts of useless loot . Crafting isn't fun either. This game has an especially weak midgame once leveling slows down, as they don't increase the spawncounts enough while increasining bullet spongelike enemies.

Personally, the only reason to play this instead of Grim Dawn if you are looking for a more accessibly gaming exprience. With slightly more colorful settings, generic fantasy themes instead of grimpunk. The passive system in this game is far easier to navigate that Grim Dawn's Devotion system. Far harder to mess up your build in this game too.

what i received was a buggy slop heap filled with mtx that performs poorly, if you're craving a arpg just go play project diablo 2, the devs over there know what they're doing and they're doing it for FREE.

Great Isometric RPG. More depth of customization than Grim Dawn, less overwhelming than Path of Exile. Each of the skills has plenty of room for personal customization.

My personal favorite ARPG on the market right now, less complicated than POE1/2, but more depth than D4. It can take a bit to get used to the systems, but it is the best loot filter in the game IMO and the skill trees are more interesting than any other ARPG. Can't recommend it enough.

This game is really good so far even though it's early access. It's got some great character customization options and the loot filter is magical and genius and the best thing to happen to the genre since the first ARPG was made.

EDIT: I've played it a lot more since I left this review. It's now my favorite game in this genre by a significant margin. I've tried playing a couple of others and after playing this one, those others all feel like crap to play. The item filtering and character customization in this are just too good. Buy now!

coming from Poe and having there well over 20k hrs. i can say last epoch is really refreshing. the game is well thought out yes there isn't as near content as in Poe but i strongly believe that the devs will continue releasing new endgame content! the game feels very responsive and has very good optimization despite playing at 1440p high i never saw a fps drop below 190 fps. the only thing i hope to see improved is loading times between areas/zones. I can only strongly suggest to my fellow Exiles to try this out!

As a fan of ARPGs this is definetely a game needs to be played. Every skill is greatly different than any other skill in the game (unlike Path Of Exile, ehm). You can specialize skills in parallel to level them up. With each skill level you change that skill drastically, it even reflects visually if possible. Every class I played was fun and unique.

Early access note: trailers of this game are horrible. Current version is not that horrible-looking. Check a recent gameplay on youtube.

Perfect game for ARPG fan. The game are pretty challenging and little rack my brains but is not as intricate and overwhelming as Path of Exile that require PhD on using spreadsheet and having the third-party program like PoB. It is also not as dull and simplicity as in Diablo 3. This is better than Grim Dawn in my opinion and the game surprisingly is still in beta.

The game is good, it still needs to get Steam Deck verified but they've done a lot of work in a year.

Optimize this thing for Steam Deck next, thanks

Top notch ARPG, still lacking some endgame but all in all very fun to play with loads of content and replayability.
One of the best crafting systems in ARPGs, and the ingame skill system is genious also!
Super fun. Not as complex as PoE and much deeper than ANY Diablo game. Highly recommend if you like ARPGs to put some time in and experiment with a build.

The game is good, you feel a real sense of progression as you go through the campaign. The classes feel nice, getting stronger as you level, the systems within the game are easy to understand and there's plenty of QoL additions for an ARPG (loot filter, autopick gold, big stash and inventory, separate bag for crafting with a button to put those mats inside that bag)

reason.text: Negative reviews in this period mostly object to paid DLC classes, which they say break an earlier promise that all DLC would be free.
Other reviews tie the criticism to Krafton's acquisition of the studio and its AI-first stance, which a PC Gamer news report on the same topic also covers.

Last Epoch players turn on the action RPG for announcing a paid DLC class, tanking its Steam reviews: 'go play Path of Exile instead'

tldr.text: Very Positive (80%): players praise the content, grind and story, while bugs and crashes are a common complaint.
Recent reviews are lower, at 61% positive over the last month, so the mood has dipped.

details.text: Veteran players are far more positive than new ones, so first impressions can differ sharply from long-term opinion.
A flagged negative surge, often called a review bomb, pushed the monthly score to 17% positive from a usual 76%, so that dip should not be read as a verdict on the game today.
